rationale: Vortioxetine (SMS; t½ ~66h; minimal sedation; cognitive benefits) to mirtazapine (NaSSA: α2-antagonist, 5-HT2/3 antagonist, H1 blocker; significant sedation and weight gain). Switch reasons: sleep problems, need for greater appetite stimulation, or after non-response. Vortioxetine self-tapers due to long half-life. Mirtazapine is 5-HT2 antagonist — combined with vortioxetine's serotonergic effects during brief overlap; low serotonin syndrome risk at standard doses but additive sedation possible. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Stop vortioxetine. Start mirtazapine 15 mg nocte. Vortioxetine levels decline gradually (t½ 66h). Counsel patient about increased sedation and appetite from mirtazapine — take at night. Weight gain is expected and can be significant.
Vortioxetine cleared. Continue mirtazapine 15 mg. Titrate to 30 mg at 2 weeks if response inadequate (30 mg is less sedating than 15 mg due to additional noradrenergic activation at higher doses).

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Vortioxetine 20 mg → mirtazapine 15 mg (start dose; target 30–45 mg). Not pharmacologically equivalent. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.
